name: Greater Hartford Reentry Welcome Center (Community Partners in Action)
description: A one-stop center where people coming home from prison get help with basic needs, ID, housing, treatment, and jobs.
notes: Hours listed Mon-Fri 8am-4pm. CPA's older /reentrywelcomecenter/ page still shows the old City Hall address; use 716 Windsor St. Serves all genders. CT Mirror (July 2025) reported intake had been paused for lack of funding; CPA said in June 2026 the state now funds the center. Call ahead to confirm intake.

name: Greater Waterbury Reentry Welcome Center (Community Partners in Action)
description: A walk-in center in Waterbury that helps people after prison with basic needs, referrals, and case management.
address: 77 Bishop Street, Ground Floor, Waterbury, CT 06704
notes: Hours listed Mon-Fri 8am-4pm. Call ahead to confirm intake (funding was unstable in 2025).

name: Bridgeport Reentry Welcome Center (Career Resources, Inc.)
description: Career Resources' center in Bridgeport that connects returning citizens to coordinated services to help them settle back into the community.
notes: The organization's page lists only a referral form, with no address or phone. An older news report gave 480 Bond St, but this is unconfirmed. CT Mirror (July 2025) reported the center might close without state funding; CPA said in June 2026 the state now funds 6 centers, including Bridgeport. Current operating status should be confirmed.

name: New Haven Reentry Welcome Center / Goodwill Reentry Initiative (Goodwill of Southern New England)
description: Goodwill's Westville site welcomes people coming home to New Haven with a welcome bag, referrals, case management, and job training.
notes: Hours Mon-Fri 8am-4pm. Case management requires a referral from DOC, Adult Probation, Federal Probation, or a community partner; unclear whether the welcome center takes walk-ins. The DOC page still lists Project M.O.R.E. as the New Haven center, but Goodwill's page now names itself the New Haven Reentry Welcome Center (the city approved a Goodwill agreement in 2025).

name: Greater New Britain Reentry Welcome Center (New Life II)
description: A faith-based, peer-led center in New Britain offering basic needs help, peer support, and referrals after release.
address: 117 West Main Street, New Britain, CT 06051
notes: Hours listed Mon-Fri 8am-4pm. The re-entry page shows ZIP 06120, which is likely a typo; the site footer uses 06051. Faith-based (Christian) program.

name: CT Department of Correction - Offender Reentry Services Unit
description: The state DOC reentry unit can help with ID held at discharge, reentry guides, and general reentry questions.
notes: Also 860-692-6836 or DOC.ORSU@ct.gov for IDs held after discharge (kept up to 2 years). This page's welcome-center list is out of date.

name: Mart's House (Community Partners in Action)
description: A 6-bedroom sober transitional home in Manchester for women moving from prison or shelter to their own place.
notes: No phone, address, or eligibility/referral process is published. Contact CPA for intake.

name: Lucy Baney Family Reunification Center (Career Resources, Inc.)
description: A DOC-funded work-release home in Bridgeport for up to 20 women, with 5 beds where mothers can live with children under 5.
notes: Program details come from Career Resources' page. Phone and address come from the DOC Directory of Contracted Community Programs (June 2024, https://portal.ct.gov/-/media/doc/pdf/rfp/directory-of-community-providers-june-2024.pdf), which lists it as STARS/Women and Children's Program. DOC referral only; 3-6 month stay.

name: Women's RISE (The Connection, Inc.)
description: A 15-bed work-release program in New Haven helping women under DOC supervision with jobs, housing plans, and recovery support.
notes: Verified only from the June 2024 DOC directory, plus current job postings showing the program is active. I did not find a program page on The Connection's site. DOC referral only.

name: Silliman House (Community Solutions, Inc.)
description: A 15-bed residential program in Hartford that helps women under DOC supervision with jobs, money skills, counseling, and housing referrals.
notes: Verified only from the June 2024 DOC directory; not confirmed on the provider's own site. DOC referral only. Lower confidence.

name: Virginia Wells Transitional House (Project M.O.R.E.)
description: A 21-bed transitional home in New Haven for women, with stays up to 6 months while in treatment and working or in school.
notes: Referral only, by a judge, Adult Probation, or Bail Commissioner (court/CSSD-funded). The phone is Project M.O.R.E.'s main line (830 Grand Ave). The house address is not published on the org site.

name: Statewide Legal Services of Connecticut
description: A free legal aid hotline and the main entry point for low-income civil legal help (family, housing, benefits, unemployment).
notes: Does not handle criminal or immigration cases. Very low income required. Online application at apply.slsct.org. Central CT line: 860-344-0380.

name: New Haven Legal Assistance Association
description: Free civil legal help in the New Haven area for family/restraining orders, housing (including criminal-record denials), benefits, and employment.
notes: Covers New Haven County and the Lower Naugatuck Valley (full town list on site). Meriden is for elderly clients only. No criminal matters.

name: Greater Hartford Legal Aid
description: Free civil legal representation for low-income people in the greater Hartford area.
notes: The org site loaded but showed no contact details. Phone and address come from search results citing the US District Court CT legal-assistance list (Aug 2025). CTLawHelp advises calling Statewide Legal Services first.

name: Connecticut Legal Services
description: Free civil legal representation for low-income people across CT outside the Hartford and New Haven areas.
notes: The phone listed is the Statewide Legal Services intake line, which CTLawHelp says is the usual entry point. Office phone numbers were not verified. Offices are in Bridgeport, Middletown, New Britain, New London, Stamford, Waterbury, and Willimantic.

name: CTLawHelp.org
description: A free website with plain-language legal self-help guides and a legal help finder for Connecticut residents.
notes: Website only.

name: Clean Slate Connecticut (automatic record erasure)
description: The state website explaining which old, low-level convictions are erased automatically and how to petition for others.
notes: Information site, not a legal clinic. Pre-2000 and cannabis erasures need a petition. The press reported in July 2026 that the backlog has cleared. No individual status-check portal was confirmed.

name: CT Board of Pardons and Paroles - Pardons (Absolute Pardon and Certificate of Employability)
description: Apply online for free for a pardon that erases your CT record, or a Certificate of Employability that helps with jobs and licenses.
notes: Eligibility waits: 3 years after a misdemeanor, 5 after a felony; no pending charges; not on probation or parole. There is no application fee, but the State Police background check costs money. A pardons phone (203-805-6643) appeared in search results but not on the page I verified, so it is left null.

name: CT DMV Non-Driver Photo ID
description: Get a state photo ID card at a DMV office if you don't have a valid driver's license.
notes: Fee is $28 (valid 7 years) and is waived for people who are unhoused or living in a shelter or transitional housing (proof needed). Requires Form B-230 and an in-person appointment; the card is mailed within 20 business days.

name: Birth Certificate Copies (CT DPH Vital Records / Town Clerk)
description: Order a certified copy of a CT birth certificate from your town of birth ($20) or the State Vital Records Office ($30).
notes: If you have no photo ID, DOC release papers with a photo dated within 12 months or probation documents count toward the two alternative IDs required. Town offices are usually faster. For births before 2003, order from the birth town, the mother's town, or the state.

name: Social Security Card Replacement (SSA)
description: Request a free replacement Social Security card online or through a local SSA office.
notes: Free. The card is mailed in 5-10 business days. TTY 1-800-325-0778. Federal resource.

name: SNAP Food Assistance (CT DSS)
description: Monthly money on an EBT card for groceries for people with low income.
notes: Apply at connect.ct.gov. Emergency cases are approved within 7 days. Federal H.R.1 work-rule changes in 2026 affect some adults; DSS has a prescreener. Local Community Action Agencies can help with applying.

name: HUSKY Health (Connecticut Medicaid/CHIP)
description: Free or low-cost health coverage for eligible adults, parents, children, and pregnant people.
notes: Apply through Access Health CT or connect.ct.gov. The phone is the DSS Benefits Center; the HUSKY-specific line was not verified. H.R.1 work rules may apply (DSS has a HUSKY prescreener).

name: Temporary Family Assistance (TFA) Cash Help (CT DSS)
description: Monthly cash help for low-income families with children, with time and income limits.
notes: Adults without children may qualify for SAGA if unable to work. Apply via connect.ct.gov. The phone is the DSS Benefits Center.

name: Care 4 Kids Child Care Subsidy (CT Office of Early Childhood)
description: Helps low- to moderate-income families pay for child care while working or in school/training.
notes: There may be an enrollment waitlist for some applicants, but TFA/JFES families have priority. Fully paperless (Parent Portal only) from Jan 1, 2027.

name: WIC Nutrition Program (CT DPH)
description: Healthy food, nutrition counseling, and breastfeeding support for pregnant/postpartum women and children under 5.
notes: People on SNAP, TFA, or HUSKY are automatically income-eligible. Citizenship is not required. Start with the online interest form or a local WIC office. The phone is the State WIC Office.

name: 2-1-1 Connecticut / Coordinated Access Network (CAN) Housing Line
description: Call 2-1-1 and press option 3 if you are homeless or about to be, to be screened and offered a CAN housing appointment.
notes: Housing option hours Mon-Fri 8:30am-4pm. TTY 1-800-671-0737. CT is not a right-to-shelter state, so shelter is not guaranteed. DV survivors should use Safe Connect.

name: Connecticut Fair Housing Center
description: Free help if you face housing discrimination or eviction, plus tenant rights self-help tools.
notes: Toll free 888-247-4401. Its site does not specifically cover criminal-record housing screening, so its help in those cases is unclear.

name: Eviction Help CT (Right to Counsel)
description: If you face eviction or loss of a housing subsidy like Section 8, you may have the right to a free lawyer.
notes: Number and site are as listed on the Statewide Legal Services homepage. I did not separately check evictionhelpct.org. Income eligibility applies.

name: American Job Centers (CT Department of Labor)
description: Free job search help, resume help, workshops, and job fairs at offices across Connecticut.
notes: The phone is CT DOL's main line. Full-service offices: Hartford 60 Weston St (860) 256-3700; Bridgeport 2 Lafayette Sq (203) 455-2700; New Haven 370 James St Ste 404 (203) 624-1493; Waterbury 249 Thomaston Ave (203) 437-3380; Montville/Uncasville (860) 848-5200. Hamden AJC is closed. There are also affiliate sites.

name: CTHires.com (state job board)
description: Connecticut's free online job board, run with the American Job Centers.
notes: Website only. It is a general job board, not fair-chance-specific.

name: BEST Chance (Capital Workforce Partners)
description: Free job training (construction, carpentry, culinary), career counseling, and support for people with criminal justice involvement in north-central CT.
address: Veeder Place, 20-28 Sargeant Street, Hartford, CT 06103
notes: Must be 18+, eligible to work in the US, and live in North Central CT. Some trainings need a HS diploma/GED. Stipends may be available.

name: Honest Jobs
description: A free national online job platform that connects people with criminal records to fair-chance employers.
notes: National, not CT-specific; the number of CT job listings is unknown. Now an Orijin company.

name: Jobs.CT.gov - Career Support for Justice-Involved People
description: A state web page listing reentry job programs in Connecticut.
notes: The page is dated Dec 2023 and some programs it links to may have ended (e.g., WE RISE Together ended June 30, 2026).

name: CT Judicial Branch Court Service Centers
description: Free help desks in courthouses for people without a lawyer, including family/custody cases.
notes: 14 locations. Search results showed Hartford Family Court CSC at (860) 706-5064; I could not load the page text directly. Hours are generally Mon-Fri 8:30am-5pm. Staff cannot give legal advice.

name: CT Department of Children and Families (DCF)
description: The state child welfare agency; if your children are in DCF care, reunification is the preferred goal when it is safe.
notes: The phone is DCF's Office of Community Relations (Mon-Fri 8am-5pm), not a reunification line. Parents with open cases should work with their assigned social worker and attorney. The Careline (1-800-842-2288) is for reporting abuse.

name: Child Support Services (CT DSS Office of Child Support Services)
description: Help establishing parentage, setting up or changing child support orders, and collecting payments.
notes: The phone is the payment line (State Disbursement Unit). Apply through a local OCSS resource center (12 statewide).

name: 988 Suicide & Crisis Lifeline
description: Call or text 988, or chat online, 24/7 for free, confidential support if you are in emotional distress or crisis.
notes: In an emergency, call or text 911.

name: CT Safe Connect (Domestic Violence Resource Line)
description: A free, confidential 24/7 line (call, text, chat, or email) for anyone affected by domestic violence, connecting to local DV services and shelter.
notes: Run by the CT Coalition Against Domestic Violence (CCADV). Spanish and ASL pages are available.

name: 2-1-1 Connecticut Crisis Line (press 1)
description: Dial 2-1-1 and press 1 for mental health or substance-use crisis support, including connection to a local mobile crisis team.
notes: The DMHAS page says 211 Infoline is certified by the American Association of Suicidology. Adults 18+; youth go through a separate youth mobile crisis route.
